messages.subject: Re: R and paired t-tests
parts:
I don't understand why you run a test involving means - why not a test
involving frequencies - how often nooze and how often nyooze in
conditions x, y, z?

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries

On Thu, Apr 1, 2010 at 14:03, Stefan Dollinger <dst...@dchp.ca> wrote:
>
> Hey there, I have hit a snag:
>
> I have two surveys and the question is whether the results are different or
> not. There are eight age cohorts and the variables are categorical (is news
> pronounced nooze or nyooze and so on).
>
> I ran t-tests based on the means for each age group, so I have 8 data points
> (the means) for Survey 1, and 8 data points for Survey 2. I ran these tests
> for all my variables (in a couple of cases there was no normal distribution,
> so I used the Wilcoxon test instead).
>
> The results looked fine. But there may be a problem.
>
> The following is evident: the 8 age cohorts do not have the same n's: they
> vary from 60 to 120 to 40 and the oldest age cohort has only 15. I've been
> trying to run the t-test on the raw data and not the means. I took the
> responses of one survey and paired them with a sample, matched by age group,
> from the other survey (which has bigger n's). My data frames look like this:
>
> FQ and PQ is the survey type, 1 & 2... the age cohort (10-year olds, 20-year
> old), and then the form (categorical).
>
> 1       FQ   1  nooze
> 2       FQ   1 nyooze
> 3       FQ   1 nyooze
> 4       FQ   2  nooze
> 5       FQ  2 nyooze
> 6       FQ  2 nyooze
>
> 168     PQ   1  nooze
> 169     PQ   1 nyooze
> 170     PQ   1 nyooze
> 171     PQ   2 nyooze
> 172     PQ   2 nyooze
> 173     PQ   2 nyooze
>
> I ran the procedures in the Gries book (Shapiro Wilk, then t.test)
>
> R gives an error message:
>
>> t.test(Survey~News, paired=T, data=News)
> Error in complete.cases(x, y) : not all arguments have the same length
>
> Any thoughts? I'd appreciate your help.
>
> Stef
>
>
